title: Environment diagrams and closures
notes: Frames
A frame holds local name bindings and a link to its parent frame. Name lookup checks the current frame before following the parent link.
Closure
A closure is a function together with the environment captured where it was defined. The function remembers that parent even after the outer call returns.
Higher-order function
A higher-order function takes a function as input or returns a function. In make_adder, the returned function remembers the number in its defining frame.

title: Recursion, call trees, and memoization
notes: Base case
Every recursive function needs a base case that returns without another recursive call. The recursive case must move toward that base case.
Tree recursion
Tree recursion makes multiple recursive calls in one frame. Naive Fibonacci repeats the same subproblems, so its call tree grows exponentially.
Memoization
Memoization caches results by input. When Fibonacci asks for a value already computed, the cache replaces a whole branch with a lookup.

title: Graphs and breadth-first search
notes: Graph
A graph represents entities as vertices and relationships as edges. An adjacency list stores the neighbors of each vertex without a full matrix.
Breadth-first search
Breadth-first search explores a graph one layer at a time using a queue. In an unweighted graph, the first discovered route uses the fewest edges.
Visited set
Mark a vertex visited when adding it to the queue. This prevents cycles from creating repeated work and keeps traversal linear in vertices plus edges.

title: Midterm review: choosing the right abstraction
notes: Closure
A closure answers what environment a function remembers. Draw the defining frame and parent links before tracing any calls.
Memoization
Memoization answers which subproblems repeat. Use input values as cache keys and compare the number of distinct states with the recursion tree.
Breadth-first search
Breadth-first search answers how to explore an unweighted graph by distance. Trace the queue and visited set together to explain the shortest path.

title: Sampling and confidence intervals
notes: Sampling variability
A sample statistic changes across repeated samples. Larger random samples generally reduce its standard error, but cannot repair a biased sampling process.
Confidence interval
A confidence interval comes from a procedure with a stated long-run coverage rate. It is not a probability that the fixed parameter moves inside this particular interval.
Standard error
The standard error describes variability of an estimate across samples. For a sample mean with independent observations, it scales with the inverse square root of sample size.

title: Experiments, effect sizes, and decisions
notes: Random assignment
Random assignment balances potential confounders in expectation. Keep the assigned groups intact when estimating the effect of offering the treatment.
Effect size
An effect size measures the magnitude of a difference. Report an interval with the estimate so readers can distinguish practical importance from statistical evidence.
Confidence interval
A narrow confidence interval indicates a more precise estimate under the model assumptions. It does not automatically imply a useful effect or an unbiased experiment.

title: Billing migration: launch readiness
notes: Feature flag
We agreed to release the billing migration behind a feature flag. The initial release must not change customer invoices until the cutover review is complete.
Proration risk
Priya owns the proration tests. Priya will test upgrades, downgrades, and cancel-then-resubscribe by Thursday. Duplicate invoices are a blocker for launch.

notes: Proration risk
Priya completed the upgrade and downgrade cases. Cancel-then-resubscribe still needs a regression test, so the team agreed to keep the feature flag off.

notes: Launch decision

Rollback plan

title: Customer discovery: onboarding friction
notes: Activation
Three research participants could not find the first project action. We agreed that the next prototype should make creating a project the primary onboarding step.
Experiment
Lena will build two onboarding variants by Tuesday. Compare completion and time to first project; do not treat a faster click as proof of long-term retention.
Research risk
The participants were existing customers, so this evidence may not represent new signups. Omar will recruit new users for the next study by Friday.

title: Prototype review: simplify the first session
notes: Activation
We agreed to test one primary action and defer optional setup. The prototype now shows a sample project so a new user can understand the result before starting.
Experiment
Lena will instrument time to first project by Thursday. Omar will review the experiment plan before recruitment begins.
Success criteria
A successful first session means completing a meaningful project action, not merely closing onboarding. The team has not yet agreed on a numeric launch threshold.

title: Weekly review: insights into next steps
notes: Research result
New participants found the primary action more easily in the revised prototype. This is qualitative evidence from a small sample, not a measured conversion lift.
Next experiment
We agreed to run a randomized experiment after instrumentation is reviewed. Lena will verify assignment tracking by Monday, and Omar will check the analysis plan.
Open question
What minimum effect would justify shipping? The team needs to agree on practical effect size before examining results. Confidence intervals will communicate uncertainty.
